what_happened: The job to refuse readings that use a delivery verb but name no user-visible outcome was rejected at the final verdict. There were two major findings and no blockers. First, the changelog says all three cited jobs were delivery-verb misreads, but only one was. The new check fires for that one and not for the other two, so the class is prevented for 1 of 3 recorded instances. Second, the accepted reading did not match the request, so passing criteria did not show the request was met. No checks failed, and the event lists no unmet criteria.
cause: Two things were never tied back to evidence before the final verdict. The request's premise (that three named jobs were delivery-verb misreads) was not checked against those jobs' recorded cases when the reading was accepted. The new refusal rule and its changelog claim were also never tested against the cited instances to show how many they catch. The rule and the claim were both written from the request's wording. Only the verifier, reading the finished diff, compared them with the real cases. This is the same gap as the earlier reading that misread its request.
prevention: When a request cites past jobs as the evidence for a new rule, the reading stage should pull each cited job's recorded case and write down how it was classified. A reading-refusal job should then be required to include a replay test that runs the new rule over every cited instance and states how many it catches. Any claim about coverage in the changelog or docs must equal the replay result, and a mismatch should hold the job before the producer runs. A cited job that does not fit the premise should be flagged to the person running Athena at reading time.
proposed_request: Make the reading-refusal rule for delivery-verb requests (the verb names no user-visible outcome) honest about what it covers. First, look up each job that the earlier request cited as a delivery-verb misread, and state in the job's notes which of them are real delivery-verb misreads and which belong to another class. Second, add a test that runs the check over the real recorded request and reading text of every job that truly is a delivery-verb misread, and asserts that the check refuses each one. Third, correct the CHANGELOG entry and the doc of check_outcome_state so they claim only what that test shows, and give the count (for example, 1 of 1 real instances) instead of saying all three. Acceptance: the test passes for every real instance; the changelog count matches the test; no instance is claimed that the check does not catch; the check does not refuse ordinary requests that name a user-visible outcome, shown by replaying it over past accepted readings.
